trigger: a database that already holds a foreign public.schema_migrations (golang-migrate, Rails, Flyway)
summary: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS skipped the foreign table silently, the next SELECT of sha256 failed, and run() returned false for every store at boot with an error that did not name the collision. Reproduced. FIXED: the table is public.yuzu_schema_migrations everywhere; a test runs the runner beside a foreign table.
classification_rationale: the diff presented the table as the runner's own; it could be someone else's

trigger: a later change weakens the skip-branch compare or the per-store TOFU lock
summary: Every test ran on one connection, so removing the apply-loop skip-branch compare or the TOFU lock left the suite green. FIXED: a threaded case (same vector, competing text over five rounds, concurrent pre-table TOFU) with a start latch and no sleeps.
classification_rationale: a required test deliverable was absent

trigger: the DDL becomes conditional or loses IF NOT EXISTS
summary: The pre-table section only deleted rows, so the real upgrade shape (schema_meta present, table absent) was never exercised. FIXED: a DROP TABLE section.
classification_rationale: a required test was absent

trigger: a production database reaches the refusal and the operator follows upgrading.md
summary: The note said to restore this build's own backup, but a drifted database's backup reproduces the refusal, and no other exit was given. FIXED: start the build that applied the migration, or restore a backup taken under this build into a fresh deployment; keep the log line; open an issue; do not edit the table; #3895 is the source-side guard.
classification_rationale: the guidance did not work for the case it was written for

trigger: the database role lacks a privilege the runner now needs, or the connection drops during the read
summary: The note told the operator to restart for a permission error, which a restart cannot fix, and did not state the privileges. FIXED: split into restart-for-transient and grant-for-permission; CREATE on public and SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on the table are stated.
classification_rationale: restart advice contradicted the failure it was attached to

adjudicated_by: architect (Gate 8 round 1), security-guardian (Gate 8 round 1) and sre (Gate 8 round 1), each independent of and not the author of this change; Gate 7's separation for a rejected finding: a reviewer other than the author accepted it
adjudication_rationale: the precedent was checked in code by architect: LeaderElector::connect_locked re-runs the runner on every connect and the version-0-with-tables guard already refuses the same way on a tampered schema_meta; security-guardian: fail-closed and availability-only, needs DB write access, re-verification must be kept; sre: visible 'no leader' state, same hand-edit already trips the existing guard. The architect's check was by reading the code and did not run the version = 0 case.
trigger: an operator hand-edits the leader_elector hash row after boot; every replica's LeaderElector re-runs run() on reconnect
summary: A post-boot edit of the recorded hash makes the elector non-open on every replica, so no replica leads. DECLINED: the failure is fail-closed and loud, the trigger is an operator rewriting a bookkeeping row, and a hand-edit of public.schema_meta (version 0 with tables) already makes the elector's run() refuse through the existing guard; skipping re-verification on reconnect would open a real gap. The limit is documented (upgrading.md). The probe lock_timeout work is #7320. Not filed as an issue.
classification_rationale: the diff did not say a reconnect re-verifies; the docs now do

trigger: the ADR text is read as an author rule
summary: The ADR said every migration is built from literals or compile-time constants; instruction_store v3 is generated at first call from a fixed column list (deterministic, so the hashes are stable). FIXED: reworded to a deterministic function of fixed text, with the census (52 pure literals, six built from constants or generated).
classification_rationale: the prose contradicted the code on a stated author instruction

trigger: a row whose sha256 is 64 characters with control bytes
summary: The drift log line printed the recorded hash prefix raw, and a hand-edited or uppercase hash was reported as 'the migration text was changed'. FIXED: read_recorded_hashes refuses any value that is not 64 lowercase hex with its own message and never logs it.
classification_rationale: the message misdescribed a damaged record as drift

trigger: a reader of device_inventory_store.cpp v3
summary: The v3 comment said the runner is gated on the version number only (no checksum), which this change made false. FIXED: the comment names both paths (hash refusal after the table existed, projection check before).
classification_rationale: a comment contradicted the code

trigger: an auditor reads the ADR as CC8.1 evidence of unauthorised-change detection
summary: No document said the control detects accidental or procedural drift, not tampering by a database-privileged actor. FIXED in the header, ADR, playbook and upgrading.md.
classification_rationale: a required limitation statement was missing

trigger: a dev or UAT operator follows the reset recipe on a store whose data is evidence
summary: The do-not-drop list omitted access reviews, quarantine, tokens, engine principals, approvals and execution or response history, and the recipe gave no change-ticket note. The reviewers weighed I4 and did not derive it: the section is dev/UAT-only, tells production not to run it, and names the secrets and CA stores. FIXED: the list, restore-if-unsure, and the change-ticket note.
classification_rationale: the list read as complete and was not

trigger: a session dies between the DROP and the DELETE of the reset recipe
summary: The recipe was three separate statements. FIXED: one BEGIN..COMMIT; sre ran it on a throwaway database (a mistyped schema name rolls the whole block back).
classification_rationale: the recipe did not say it was atomic and was not

trigger: two or more drifted stores in a dev or UAT database
summary: server.cpp skips later stores once one refuses, so drift appears one store per start. FIXED: stated in upgrading.md (typically one per start; the elector re-checks on reconnect). Impact is I8, not I5: the refusal itself is the intended behaviour; the finding is that drift is discovered one store at a time.
classification_rationale: a required operator note was missing

trigger: two processes boot the same pre-table store at once
summary: The second process logged 'trust on first use' for zero rows. FIXED: return before the insert loop when the re-read leaves nothing missing.
classification_rationale: a log line described a write that did not happen

trigger: none
summary: <algorithm> was included and unused. FIXED: removed (<utility> added for std::move).
classification_rationale: include hygiene

trigger: a runner that trims m.sql before hashing, or a failure that is not the read failure
summary: The unreadable-record section asserted only a false return, and no DB section pinned exact bytes. FIXED: a log assertion, and a migration with newlines and a trailing newline compared to its hash.
classification_rationale: a test oracle was weak

adjudication_rationale: accepted as INFO: the path is safe by inspection and the hash write shares the schema_meta transaction
trigger: a failed hash write mid-apply
summary: No test forces upsert_applied_hash to fail mid-apply. DECLINED: safe by inspection (PgTxn rolls the apply back, cpp-safety confirmed).
classification_rationale: an optional test

adjudication_rationale: accepted as INFO: honest edit, optional follow-up
trigger: none
summary: The enablement test deletes the hash rows instead of slicing the store's own vector; the cleaner shape needs a migrations() seam that does not exist. DECLINED as an optional follow-up; the edit models a pre-table database honestly.
classification_rationale: test shape preference

trigger: a split migrate and run role
summary: The privileges the runner now needs were not stated. FIXED with the permission advice.
classification_rationale: a required operator note was missing

trigger: a future test hand-copies a vector under a shipped store name
summary: The playbook gave test authors no rule about the hash table. FIXED: use a unique store name, slice the store's own vector, or delete that store's rows.
classification_rationale: a required author note was missing

trigger: two or more processes first-boot the same store at once
summary: The version-0-with-tables guard (#1320) read the version without the per-store lock, so a runner that read 0 just before a concurrent first boot committed saw that boot's tables and refused spuriously; the new concurrency case hit it about 1 run in 10 (reproduced 3/30). FIXED: re-read the version before refusing (the tables and the version row commit in one transaction, so a re-read after the tables are visible cannot miss a committed version); 0 failures in 60 runs, 7 in 40 with the re-read reverted. Gate 8 round 2: architect, cpp-safety and quality-engineer found no defect.
classification_rationale: ADR-0012 treats a concurrent first boot as safe and the guard contradicted it

trigger: a reader of the #3894 text after a downgrade onto edited text
summary: The #3894 header, playbook, upgrading.md and WARN text still said the ahead case only warns and returns true, but the hash check that follows can refuse. FIXED: each says the ahead check itself only warns and the recorded-hash check can still refuse.
classification_rationale: prose contradicted the code

trigger: an operator runs DROP SCHEMA <store> CASCADE where other schemas depend on it
summary: sre reproduced CASCADE silently dropping a foreign key and a view in another schema. FIXED: a clause to read the NOTICE before COMMIT; the store name is the schema name; an ERROR rolls the block back.
classification_rationale: the recipe said it deletes one store's data

trigger: a reader of the ADR census and the playbook sentence
summary: The census read 52 + six + one against 58 vectors, and a playbook sentence cited #3013 for a limit it does not describe. FIXED.
classification_rationale: wording

trigger: the CI format check
summary: The rename pushed several lines past the 100-column limit. FIXED: clang-format on the new lines.
classification_rationale: formatting

trigger: a reader of the playbook Runner-guards bullet
summary: The bullet said a version-0 schema with tables is refused, understating the re-read. FIXED: refused when the version is still 0 on a re-read; a concurrent first boot that commits between the reads is adopted. Impact is I8, not I7: the bullet exists and is correct for a persistent version 0; it only understated the re-read.
classification_rationale: prose understated the code

trigger: a red run of the concurrency section read as noise
summary: The case catches a removed re-read about 1 run in 6 and nothing can force the interleaving without a production hook. ACCEPTED as probabilistic; FIXED: a comment saying a red run is the re-read gone.
classification_rationale: a limit the test should state
